subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: We'd been on the road south out of the Silver Marches long enough that I'd stopped counting days and started counting how much my boots hurt.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: hill giant count
fact: The hill giants I grew up with had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.
source_quote: The hill giants I grew up with — they had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern was noted for later but not entered immediately.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, was mounted on a stone pillar as a monument to Tarvis Ulain.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar.

subject: pewter hand cast value
fact: The pewter hand casts were charm-sized and sold for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: Daz's inscription discovery
fact: Daz found a Dwarven inscription on the base of the monument reading 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Milo Goodbarrel's witness
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, head of a publisher, witnessed and recorded the monument for the Gauntlet.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild funding
fact: The monument was funded two years after the war by the Metalworkers Guild.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Elin's silence
fact: Elin, age 7, had been silent for 6 days and drew a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: Dawnbringer's restoration
fact: Dawnbringer performed lesser restoration on Elin, after which she spoke: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: Lesser restoration settled in. And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Daz's head pressure
fact: Daz had been experiencing pressure in his head, possibly linked to the same phenomenon affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn was named after a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued.

subject: wall memory
fact: The south wall of the inn remembers where the wizard fell; it is not painted over.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: bard's song 'The Kenku Could Not Fly'
fact: A bard performed 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' a song about a thief who stole only what was needed.
source_quote: This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'

subject: Whistler's restraint
fact: Whistler, a Kenku thief, took only what was necessary from Tiamat's hoard, making a line-item budget.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Daz's mental state
fact: Daz's condition originated below ground and persists on the surface, suggesting a lingering effect of Underdark madness.
source_quote: Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: Candlekeep architecture
fact: Candlekeep is a centuries-old structure whose presence defies casual observation, embodying endurance and silent authority.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: spy's imprisonment request
fact: The spy demanded formal incarceration by Candlekeep, but was denied because her status as a party member placed decision-making authority with the adventuring group.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: Glabbagool's prisoner interaction
fact: Glabbagool has developed a routine of conflict and meditation with the spy, treating her as a reluctant student in the art of stillness under provocation.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream.

subject: Glabbagool's monkhood question
fact: Glabbagool asked Zalthir whether watching the spy would make him more or less of a monk, and received affirmation that this was intentional training.
source_quote: Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?

subject: Zalthir's trial structure
fact: Khell-Vire's trial of Zalthir reframed assessment from knowledge to transformation, asking not what Zalthir knew but what he had become.
source_quote: What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?

subject: blind monk's assessment
fact: The blind monk judged Zalthir's techniques as technically incorrect but pragmatically superior, noting that Zalthir arrived faster than the Grandmaster despite violating scrolls.
source_quote: You skip the third breath... It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: Zalthir's unconventional training
fact: Zalthir's survival in the Underdark constituted a curriculum distinct from formal shadow monk training, rendering standard rubrics irrelevant to his abilities.
source_quote: You have learned nothing." / "I survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall in Candlekeep's north inner ward returns sound altered, as if the architecture itself is taking notes.
source_quote: Stone corridors... have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Khell-Vire's note
fact: A note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.' Neither he nor Zalthir can place its origin.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: Zalthir's response to assessment
fact: Zalthir responded to the monk's critique not with defensiveness but with a flat, weary acknowledgment of the absurdity of formal evaluation against lived experience.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends.

subject: Thorin's observation
fact: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent about his role as prisoner-watcher, prompting deeper philosophical inquiry.
source_quote: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Zalthir's internal calculus
fact: Zalthir assessed whether his trial could get worse, and correctly anticipated that it could — and did.
source_quote: His internal calculus was already doing the math on whether this could get worse. It could.

subject: Candlekeep's prisoner policy
fact: Candlekeep holds prisoners only as a temporary delay, never as punishment; they are eventually released with a warning, never executed or surrendered.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them. If you give her to us, what you are giving us is a delay.

subject: the spy's emotional state
fact: The spy reacted with fury to being denied formal imprisonment, revealing her deep need for institutional recognition of her status.
source_quote: She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: Zalthir's decision on Glabbagool
fact: Zalthir affirmed that Glabbagool's watch over the spy was intentional pre-monk training, validating the chaos as discipline.
source_quote: Absolutely," I said. "It was. Patience under provocation... If anything, the spy was giving him a better curriculum than most of what I'd sat through.

subject: the monk's final judgment
fact: The blind monk concluded Zalthir had learned nothing — not because he failed, but because he had never been taught what the system valued.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: Candlekeep's bell tower cells
fact: The bell tower contains comfortable, localized anti-magic cells, rarely used, reserved for those deemed guilty of major offenses.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used.

subject: Zalthir's trial outcome
fact: Zalthir passed no formal test, but demonstrated a deeper mastery of adaptation over orthodoxy, leaving the monk without a valid rubric to judge him.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: the spy's meditation attempts
fact: The spy screamed at Glabbagool's attempts to teach her meditation, yet continued to engage with him — suggesting a hidden, reluctant openness.
source_quote: She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk.

subject: Zalthir's silence
fact: Zalthir did not explain his actions during the trial, nor did he defend himself — his silence was his answer.
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat: 'Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?'

subject: the scholar's chant
fact: A young human scholar in the Burning Wizard Inn was reciting a rhythmic, liturgical chant with a subtle, deliberate syncopation error — one Zalthir recognized as identical to a pattern seen in two others, one of whom went insane.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: the Wall's memory
fact: The soot mark on the south wall of the Burning Wizard Inn and the scrubbed floor reflect a quiet permanence — the inn remembers what its patrons forget.
source_quote: The wall remembers. I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: Thorin's sea encounter
fact: Thorin found peace in Dawnbringer’s light defeating the purpose of watching the sea — an irony he accepted as part of life’s strange directions.
source_quote: He apparently found this peaceful rather than counterproductive, which I note without judgment.

subject: Zalthir's rooftop meditation
fact: Zalthir returned from meditating on the roof with the expression of someone who had resolved an internal argument — not initiated an external one.
source_quote: He said 'Hmm, true,' about something, in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.

subject: Daz's silence
fact: Daz fell silent during the approach to Candlekeep, his hand going to his temple — a sign that his condition, rooted in the Underdark, had not abated.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: the scholar's category error
fact: The narrator consciously distinguishes 'a human scholar' from 'a young human scholar,' recognizing the latter as meaningfully different — a reflection of lived precision over abstract categorization.
source_quote: not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things and I did not want to get the category wrong

subject: the narrator's cognitive friction
fact: The narrator experienced a specific cognitive friction — the pressure of near-recognition — triggered by the scholar’s chant, linking it to past trauma and madness.
source_quote: I will call it the specific cognitive friction of almost-recognition — something pressing at the edge of attention that wants to be resolved.

subject: the spy's final status
fact: The spy remains in the party’s custody, not imprisoned, not released — held as a delay, a living question.
source_quote: We kept her.

subject: the narrator's journal closure
fact: The narrator closed his journal after documenting the chant’s pattern — not because he had answers, but because he had recognized a threat that might not yet be understood.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence... Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group... or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: the scholar's chant origin
fact: The scholar’s chant mirrors a pattern previously observed in two individuals — one of whom went insane — suggesting a contagious or inherited mental corruption.
source_quote: Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: the narrator's sun attribution
fact: The narrator had attributed his cognitive friction to sunlight — a false explanation that persisted for days, masking a deeper, more dangerous truth.
source_quote: I had been attributing it to sunlight. I had, in fact, been attributing it to sunlight for most of the day.

subject: the spy's identity
fact: The spy is a miniaturized House T'sarran operative, not a mere prisoner — her existence is a geopolitical liability.
source_quote: miniaturized House T'sarran spy

subject: the monk's blindness
fact: The blind monk’s inability to see renders traditional assessment tools useless — forcing evaluation based on outcome, not form.
source_quote: The monk was blind, so the spider gambit was dead on arrival.

subject: the First Reader's sympathy
fact: The First Reader regarded the spy with sympathy — recognizing her as a victim of circumstance, not merely a tool of House T'sarran.
source_quote: The First Reader looked at her with something that might have been sympathy

subject: the scholar's chant as doctrine
fact: The scholar’s chant may not be a ritual, but a corrupted fragment of a doctrine — one that has caused madness in others.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong, and the specific wrongness of it...

subject: Zalthir's silence as wisdom
fact: Zalthir’s refusal to defend his methods, or explain his training, is not ignorance — it is the quiet mastery of one who has lived beyond doctrine.
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat...

subject: the spy's desire for incarceration
fact: The spy’s demand to be jailed reveals a psychological need for structure — even if it is punitive — suggesting she has internalized the system’s logic.
source_quote: She delivered this the way someone delivers a thing they have never had to argue for.

subject: the narrator's self-awareness
fact: The narrator recognizes that his own perception of reality — his categorizations, his attributions — are flawed, yet he continues to observe precisely because of that flaw.
source_quote: I have been cataloguing the room during all of this, which is not something I do consciously anymore. It is just what happens when I sit somewhere new...

subject: the scholar's age and role
fact: The scholar is not merely a student — he is a young human scholar, a category distinct from adult scholars, implying a unique vulnerability or potential.
source_quote: not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things

subject: Candlekeep's institutional neutrality
fact: Candlekeep refuses to serve as an instrument of House T'sarran or any external power — it holds only what it deems necessary, and releases the rest.
source_quote: We will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her.

subject: the spy's relationship with Glabbagool
fact: The spy’s repeated attempts to kill Glabbagool have become a ritual of mutual provocation — a twisted form of teaching.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream.

subject: the monk's final walk
fact: The blind monk walked away after declaring Zalthir had learned nothing — a gesture that was not defeat, but a recognition that Zalthir had passed a test no rubric could measure.
source_quote: The monk sighed again and walked away.

subject: Thorin's question about the 30
fact: Thorin’s question — 'Does that get me anything?' — reveals his pragmatic, rule-of-thumb approach to roleplaying, contrasting with Zalthir’s existential one.
source_quote: Zalthir: 'I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?'

subject: the narrator's final realization
fact: The narrator understands that wisdom and resignation are indistinguishable — and that life’s strange directions are not problems to solve, but patterns to endure.
source_quote: I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: the wall's permanence
fact: The soot mark on the south wall and the scrubbed floor represent the quiet persistence of place — the inn remembers what its guests forget.
source_quote: The wall remembers. I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: the spy's emotional arc
fact: The spy moves from fury at denial of imprisonment to reluctant engagement with Glabbagool — suggesting a hidden, unacknowledged need for connection.
source_quote: She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk.

subject: the scholar's chant as corruption
fact: The scholar’s chant is not an accident — it is a corrupted echo of a doctrine that has driven others to madness, and may be spreading.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: Zalthir's training philosophy
fact: Zalthir believes true training is not found in scrolls, but in enduring hostile environments — a belief validated by his survival of the Underdark.
source_quote: I survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Khell-Vire's role
fact: Khell-Vire is not a teacher — he is a gatekeeper, offering Zalthir a door and refusing to walk through it, forcing him to face the trial alone.
source_quote: I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.

subject: the narrator's journal
fact: The narrator’s journal is not a record of facts, but a repository of patterns — of madness, of memory, of silent truths that cannot be spoken aloud.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: the spy's existential crisis
fact: The spy’s demand for incarceration reveals a crisis of identity — she does not know whether she is a tool, a prisoner, or a person.
source_quote: She delivered this the way someone delivers a thing they have never had to argue for.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool, a grey ooze, has become a student of patience — his transformation is not physical, but philosophical.
source_quote: I will keep an eye on her!

subject: the blind monk's wisdom
fact: The blind monk’s judgment — that Zalthir has learned nothing — is not an insult, but a revelation: he has learned what cannot be taught.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: the narrator's epiphany
fact: The narrator realizes that his own cognitive friction — the near-recognition — is not about the chant, but about his own past trauma, now mirrored in another.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong...

subject: Candlekeep's purpose
fact: Candlekeep is not a library of knowledge, but a sanctuary of silence — a place where the unspeakable is held, not solved.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: the scholar's chant as a warning
fact: The scholar’s chant is a living warning — a fragment of a corrupted doctrine that has already claimed two minds, and may claim more.
source_quote: Eldred had it... The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: Zalthir's acceptance
fact: Zalthir does not seek validation — he accepts that his path is invisible to the system, and that is enough.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends.

subject: the narrator's final line
fact: The narrator closes his journal not because he has answers, but because he has recognized a pattern that may be spreading — and he will not be the one to sound the alarm.
source_quote: I wrote it down... Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

fact: One drow is being tortured by a sentient gelatinous cube.

subject: resonant slime source
fact: A vial of Resonant Slime was produced by a sage of xenobiology.
source_quote: produced a vial of Resonant Slime

subject: eldritch tattoo value
fact: The eldritch tattoo on Zalthir's skin allows shadow tentacle growth.
source_quote: the eldritch tattoo. 'I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.'

subject: shadow step and hit combination
fact: Zalthir's combination of shadow step and hit redeems his lack of skills in all other areas.
source_quote: your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas

subject: dawnbringer identity
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who requires light and mourning to heal.
source_quote: she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight... she needs to grieve

subject: menzoberranzan ledger system
fact: Menzoberranzan trains its citizens to maintain ledgers of debts, knowledge, and losses.
source_quote: The first thing Menzoberranzan trains you for is the ledger

subject: house destruction protocol
fact: In Menzoberranzan, a house that fails to kill every member of a target house is forfeit.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child... your house was forfeit

subject: blithering idiot survivor
fact: One blithering child idiot survived the destruction of a noble house in Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: a child. A blithering child idiot, she said

subject: hall of divination atmosphere
fact: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and residual spell energy.
source_quote: smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times

subject: information exchange protocol
fact: In Candlekeep, information is exchanged reciprocally: ask for knowledge, provide knowledge.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side

subject: drow memory loss
fact: The drow narrator has no memory of his past before being imprisoned in a cell with others.
source_quote: I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail

subject: word misfit recognition
fact: Menzoberranzan trains its citizens to notice when a word doesn't fit in their social grammar.
source_quote: the second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for... is to notice when a word doesn't fit

subject: zalthir's shadow technique
fact: Zalthir chose option C of the three specialized shadow techniques offered by Khell-Vire.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C

subject: philemon's study atmosphere
fact: Master Archivist Philemon's study smells like old ink and faint mineral residue.
source_quote: smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral

subject: dawnbringer's darkness trauma
fact: Dawnbringer experienced deep unease from three to four thousand years of darkness exposure.
source_quote: sustained darkness exposure of approximately three to four thousand years

subject: thorin's pocket drow
fact: Thorin refers to a drow as 'Pocket Drow' in the context of a sentient gelatinous cube's companion.
source_quote: Pocket Drow

subject: zalthir's shadow punch
fact: Zalthir demonstrated a technique to punch through shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut.
source_quote: a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut

subject: candlekeep library policy
fact: Candlekeep enforces a policy of reciprocal information exchange.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter

subject: khell-vire's observation
fact: Khell-Vire observed that Zalthir's unorthodox technique is the most interesting thing about him.
source_quote: what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his

subject: drow narrator's truth disclosure
fact: The drow narrator disclosed his memory loss and uncertain identity to Sister Yvenne in Candlekeep.
source_quote: I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts

subject: drow survivor count
fact: One drow survivor of a destroyed noble house may be the narrator himself.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The second seat was struck.
source_quote: The second seat.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The fourth seat struck.
source_quote: The fourth seat struck.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The eleventh seat was struck.
source_quote: The eleventh seat.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The twenty-third seat was struck.
source_quote: The twenty-third seat.

subject: heraldry book age
fact: The heraldry book *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* is two hundred years old, give or take.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, give or take.

subject: footnote removal time
fact: The footnote in the heraldry book was removed by a razor at least fifty years ago.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago

subject: Yvenne's body language duration
fact: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.
source_quote: for the last five minutes
